title: Aivu, grandson of Rav
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Sukkah 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.44b.5), Aivu and Chizkiyah, the sons of Rav’s daughter, brought a willow branch before Rav. As Hyman explains in his article on Rav, he also identifies the grandson with the Aivu mentioned [on the same folio](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.44b.8) who, in the reading Hyman follows, spoke in the name of R’ Elazar bar Yitzchak.

notes.text: The supplied source has the malformed כרתיה. The consulted Sukkah paragraph reads בני ברתיה, “sons of his daughter,” supporting the bracketed translation rather than a person named Kartiah. Its other Aivu reports Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok, whereas Hyman here writes bar Yitzchak; that discrepancy remains unresolved.
The supplied כרתיה differs from ברתיה in the printed notice and the Gemara. The translation follows the printed wording “sons of his daughter.”

[Hyman’s printed notice](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._I._1910.pdf#page=169) has בני ברתיה, “sons of his daughter,” as does the Gemara. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=388&lang=en) also lists the two grandsons. The linked Gemara names Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok in Aivu’s separate transmission, while [Dikdukei Soferim](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/DQhNAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=RA2-PA137) records bar Yitzchak and [Hyman’s article on Rav](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._I._1910.pdf#page=47) argues for identifying that Aivu as the grandson. The variants leave the identification open.
